description: sessiontools' hooks, installed with the plugin. PostToolBatch: settle-hook, the settle alert. Once per model turn that calls a tool, it says AT MOST ONE line, from the `session` settings' settle block, read LIVE through the cascade on every batch (~/.sessionkit/tools/settings/session.json, agent front matter, seats/<seat>/settings/, sessions/<sid>/settings/): an edited layer is heard at the next batch. UNSET IS SILENT, ALWAYS, and settle: null in a layer switches it off. BIRTH-ONLY: the shim needs CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID (claude sets it in every hook) and that session's dir (<sessions>/<sid>), and exits 0 before python starts without either, so a session session start did not launch is silent even when a host layer sets settle. CHEAP WHEN OFF: an OFF stamp, <session dir>/settle/off, back-dated 1 s and listing every layer path the cascade read or looked for (each layer's file, the agent file, each .d folder and its files), lets the shim exit 0 by builtins, with no python, until a listed path is newer; session start writes it at birth, and a settle that turns on removes it. A file moved into a .d folder is seen (the folder's mtime changes); a top-level layer file put in place with an OLD mtime (mv, cp -p) is not, until touched. The soft line (settle.soft.at, settle.soft.every, settle.soft.say) speaks once per crossing of at + k*every, or every batch from at when every is unset; the hard line (settle.hard.at, settle.hard.before_compact, settle.hard.every, settle.hard.say) starts at the lower of at and the SET compaction point less before_compact, and speaks every batch, or once per crossing of each every. One line per batch: the hard line wins, and past it the soft line is silent. Crossings are O_EXCL marks under <session dir>/settle/, and a count that falls (a compaction) re-arms the marks above it. {at}, {used}, {compact_at} and {left} are filled; {compact_at} and {left} come only from the point the launch set, and read ? when it is unknown. The environment is not a layer: SESSION_SETTLE_AT and SESSION_SETTLE_SAY reach it only as session start's birth copy into the session layer, so a shell-rc export beats every seat. No filter on who the session is: any session whose settings set a line is told. A subagent's batch (payload agent_id) is silent. It reads the count with sessiontools.window.scan on the payload's transcript once this batch's own assistant row is there: the hook can start before that row is written, so when the payload names its tool calls it waits for the row, at most 1 s, then counts what is on disk. Otherwise it never blocks, and fails SILENT: no python3, python older than 3.11, a missing transcript, an unreadable settings file or a crash all exit 0 with no output (hooks/settle-hook, sessiontools.settle). PreCompact (matcher auto): settle-hook precompact, the COMPACTION GUARD, the belt under idleCompaction: false. When the session's settle block is ON (read live through the same cascade) and the compaction point the launch SET is known (the point {compact_at} reads, never inferred), it SKIPS an AUTO compaction (trigger: auto, an idle compaction included) whose context count is BELOW that point and is the whole context (no message after the last usage row, as when the turn is over: a threshold compaction mid-turn has the new prompt or tool results after it, which that row does not count, so it passes): exit 2, with one reason line on stderr, which Claude Code shows as 'Compaction blocked by PreCompact hook'. An auto compaction at or above the point passes. A MANUAL compaction (/compact) always passes. Settle off (unset, or settle: null), an unknown point, a transcript with no reading, a subagent's payload (agent_id) or any failure: exit 0 with no output, a no-op (a PreCompact hook's stdout would join the summary's instructions), and while the OFF stamp is fresh no python starts. The skip is measured live on the threshold path only; that it holds on the idle path is static reading, UNMEASURED (hooks/settle-hook, sessiontools.settle_guard). PostToolBatch: clock-hook, the clock line, OFF BY DEFAULT: with SESSIONTOOLS_HOOK_CLOCK=on (or 1/true/yes) in the environment it says on every batch the time and this session's context as used/max (`[clock] 12:34 UTC | ctx 182K/1.00M (18%)`; `ctx 182K/?` when the window is unknown, `ctx ?` with no reading), and no warn line: SESSION_CLOCK_WARN_AT is retired and never read, since a seat hears one warning, the settle alert's; with no mail count, the same batch-row wait and count as settle-hook, a subagent's batch silent, off exiting 0 before python starts, and any failure exiting 0 with no output (hooks/clock-hook, sessiontools.clockline). PreToolUse, PostToolBatch, Stop (verb stop), UserPromptSubmit, SessionEnd: busy-sound, the busy sound. It plays a sound file once a tool batch has run past a delay, and stops it the moment the batch returns. SILENT UNLESS SET: the `sounds` settings (~/.sessionkit/tools/settings/sounds.json, agent front matter, seats/<seat>/settings/, sessions/<sid>/settings/) need enabled: true and busy.{auto_arm: true, file, delay}. A seat without them starts python once per session (at its first tool; at its first Stop when that comes first), then pays a few stat calls per tool and per Stop. busy.trigger picks ONE mode: batch (unset; these hooks), landed or finished (signalled, not hooked: `session sound landed|given` plays and stops landed on sounds/unread; finished is held); any other value is silent in every mode, and a seat whose trigger is not batch is OFF for these hooks, paying what a seat without the setting pays. SESSIONTOOLS_HOOK_BUSY=off (or 0/false/no) switches it off with the plugin still loaded. A subagent's batch makes no sound. The player is afplay, in a detached process group that the batch end kills; end and clear stop every slot (busy, unread, finished). busy.player picks who plays the batch trigger's sound: afplay (unset) or engine, the resident sound engine. With engine, the session's first arm starts python once to write the engine's record (sounds/busy/engine.<claude pid>) and send arm; every later hook sends ONE OSC datagram (/sound/event ,ssd EVENT SID T) to UDP 127.0.0.1:44100 with the native sender (<sound home>/bin/sound-event: SESSIONTOOLS_SOUND_HOME, else the sound leaf of tools' state as sessiontools.settings resolves it, old folder while it is real), with no python and no wait (a Stop still starts python when a stop sound is set). Not installed, or an engine that is off, is silent; any other player value is silent in every mode. Stop (verb stop) also plays the STOP SOUND, after it clears the slots: with enabled: true and stop.file set, it queues that file ONCE per Stop through the mouth's queue (mouth play FILE, so it lands after any line still speaking), and plays it with afplay only when the mouth is absent, exits non-zero or cannot be run; a mouth that times out or is killed by a signal is not followed by afplay, so it never plays twice. The play runs in a detached process group, so the hook never waits for it, and no clear cuts it: it is not a slot. Unset, a bad value or a subagent's Stop is silent. An OFF stamp, sounds/stop/off, back-dated and invalidated by a newer host- or session-layer sounds file as sounds/busy/off is, keeps a seat without it from starting python at Stop; the first arm writes it too. It never blocks, and fails SILENT (hooks/busy-sound, sessiontools.busy). The same busy-sound hooks keep the TURN-ENDED MARK, so a seat whose turn is over while a background agent runs reads `idle with children`, not busy. DEFAULT OFF: nothing is written unless SESSIONTOOLS_HOOK_TURN=on (or 1/true/yes) is in the seat's environment; switching it on is a config change. On: Stop writes <sessions>/<sid>/turn-ended (the sessions leaf as sessiontools.settings resolves it, under SESSIONS_DIR when set; only when the session dir exists) atomically, one JSON line {"v": 1, "at": <epoch s>, "harness": "claude-code", "event": "Stop", "background": <running background_tasks, or null>}; PreToolUse, UserPromptSubmit and SessionEnd unlink it. An event whose payload carries agent_id (a subagent's) changes nothing. The mark runs before every sound switch and fast path, costs one stat on PreToolUse when there is no mark, never blocks, and fails SILENT (hooks/busy-sound, sessiontools.turn). PreToolUse (matcher Bash): sed-guard, the sed guard, ON BY DEFAULT. It refuses a Bash call that runs sed -i '' (BSD sed's in-place form: -i, a short-flag cluster ending in i such as -Ei, or --in-place, followed by a SEPARATE empty argument, '' or "") when the sed the call runs is GNU sed, where '' becomes the script and the call fails with exit 2. It PARSES the command, never greps it: heredoc bodies are cut, then shlex tokenises it into simple commands, so a quoted string, a heredoc body or a comment that holds the text never refuses; a word whose basename is sed or gsed anywhere in a simple command counts (xargs sed, find -exec sed). Only GNU is refused: the sed the call names is asked --version (a path at that path, a bare sed as the first on the hook's PATH; gsed is GNU), so a BSD-first host, or /usr/bin/sed -i '' on a GNU-first one, passes. The refusal is Claude Code's PreToolUse JSON on stdout, permissionDecision: deny, exit 0 (measured on 2.1.325 under bypassPermissions), and its reason names the GNU form, cut from the original text (the empty argument and the blank before it deleted, every other byte kept). SESSIONTOOLS_HOOK_SED=off (or 0/false/no) switches it off before python starts. A payload with no sed, or with no empty quote pair, starts no python. It fails OPEN and SILENT: an unbalanced quote, a probe that fails or runs past 1 s, no python3, python older than 3.11 or a crash all exit 0 with no output (hooks/sed-guard, sessiontools.sed_guard). SessionStart (verbs title, context, identity): session-info, the session-info hooks. Title and context are DEFAULT OFF, each on its own switch, checked before python starts. SESSIONTOOLS_HOOK_TITLE=on (or 1/true/yes): title sets the session title to the first 8 characters of the session id, on startup, resume and fork (or no source); never on clear or compact, where Claude Code does not apply a title, and never over a title the session already has (payload session_title, from --name, /rename or another hook). Because the title counts as a custom title, a bare /clear keeps it: the new session shows the previous short id, and a later resume keeps that title too. If a fork inherits its parent's title, the fork shows the parent's short id the same way; that is the harness's behaviour, not measured here. SESSIONTOOLS_HOOK_SESSION_INFO=on (or 1/true/yes): context injects a short Session Info block, one line each for the session id, working directory, source and transcript path, on every source; an absent or empty value is left out, and a block left with no line is not emitted. On startup (or no source) the Session ID line is left out when SESSIONTOOLS_LAUNCH_INFO equals the session id: session start exports it when the launch-info it injected carries that id. On every other source the line is printed. Identity is ON, and its switch is the file: identity injects the identity block session start wrote for this session (identity.md in the session dir, by the session resolver), byte for byte, the same text `session identity` prints, on every source; a session with no block (not launched by session start) is silent, at the cost of one python start and one failed open. SESSIONTOOLS_HOOK_IDENTITY=off (or 0/false/no) switches it off before python starts. A subagent's payload (agent_id) is silent. It never blocks, and fails SILENT: no python3, python older than 3.11, bad JSON or a crash all exit 0 with no output (hooks/session-info, sessiontools.session_info). PostToolUse (matcher Write|Edit|MultiEdit): md-lint, the Markdown lint. When the tool's file_path ends in .md (any case) it names, one line each, a table line (stripped text starts with |) of 76 or more display columns (`line 14 is 134 columns; a table line stays under 76 columns, wider lines wrap`) and the whole word shape or shapes in prose (`line 9 says 'shape': use the precise term`), under one `md-lint <path>:` header, at most 10 lines then `... and N more`. Skipped: YAML front matter, fenced code, HTML comments; for shape also code spans, links and their targets, autolinks, bare URLs, reference definitions, quoted text and blockquote lines; reshape, shaped, shaping and misshapen are other words. A Write lints the whole file; an Edit or MultiEdit lints the file on disk but reports only lines where an edit's new_string now sits. It ANSWERS, NEVER BLOCKS: additionalContext only when there is a finding, exit 0 always. ON BY DEFAULT and BIRTH-ONLY, as settle-hook: it needs CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID and that session's dir, so a session session start did not launch is silent. SESSIONTOOLS_HOOK_MD_LINT=off (or 0/false/no) switches it off before python starts, and a payload with no .md in it exits before python. It fails SILENT: no python3, python older than 3.11, bad JSON, an unreadable file or a crash all exit 0 with no output (hooks/md-lint, sessiontools.md_lint). PreToolUse (matcher Bash, verb pre) and PostToolUse (matcher Bash, verb post): hidden-failure, the hidden-failure note. A gate (pytest, python -m pytest, uv run pytest, make, message send, git commit, git push) piped into head or tail reports the reader's status, not the gate's, so a failed run can exit 0. It ADVISES ONLY, with one line of additionalContext: it never blocks, never rewrites a command and changes no exit code (no decision, no permissionDecision, no updatedInput). post: when the Bash call's last top-level pipeline, whose status reaches the call's exit (|| is never a pipe; heredoc bodies and quoted text are not code), pipes a gate into head or tail, the call exited 0, and its output (tool_response stdout + stderr) matches a failure marker, it says one line naming the gate, the reader and the marker's label, and the status-keeping form (cmd > log 2>&1; s=$?; tail log; exit $s). Exit 0 is the event itself: on Claude Code 2.1.325 a failed Bash call fires PostToolUseFailure, which is never registered here, and the note is refused when tool_response is not an object, interrupted is true, returnCodeInterpretation is set, or backgroundTaskId is set (an unknown status is not 0). pre: a gate piped into head (never tail), the same one line before the call runs. A command naming pipefail gets nothing. SEATS ONLY: unless TASKMASTER_ROLE or CLAUDE_CODE_AGENT is set and non-empty in the hook's environment, the shim exits 0 before python starts, so a human's own session is untouched; SESSIONTOOLS_HOOK_HIDDEN_FAILURE=off (or 0/false/no) switches it off on a seat. A subagent's call is NOT silenced. CHEAP: a payload with no | (and no head, or head or tail for post) exits 0 by the shell with no python, and the module is loaded by file path, not the package. PRIVATE: the note quotes no output and no command text beyond the gate's name, and nothing is logged. It fails SILENT: no python3, python older than 3.11, bad JSON or a crash all exit 0 with no output (hooks/hidden-failure, sessiontools.hidden_failure).
